evidence.finding: Offered calls jumped from 72 at 09:00 to 117 at 09:15 and remained elevated at 97–136 calls per interval through 11:45.
Incident-period demand totaled 1,308 calls against 841 forecast, approximately 56% above forecast; before 09:15, actual demand was approximately aligned with forecast.
Service level fell from 94.44% at 09:00 to 51.33% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target for every subsequent interval.
ASA rose from 19.95 seconds at 09:00 to 74.37 seconds at incident onset and reached 92.21 seconds at 09:45.
Abandonments increased to 9–42 calls per interval during the incident while answered calls remained below offered calls, indicating demand was accumulating beyond available capacity.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49 agents; productive staffing stayed between 45 and 46 agents throughout the window.
Queue staffing remained fixed at 19 General Service, 12 Billing, 11 Account Support, and 7 Escalations agents before and during the incident.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded.

primary_root_cause_detail: A sharp, sustained increase in offered calls began at 09:15. From 09:15 through 11:45, 1,308 calls were offered versus 841 forecast, approximately 56% above forecast. Available staffing remained stable, so demand exceeded effective capacity, drove occupancy to 100%, increased waits and abandonment, and depressed service level.
recommended_actions: Investigate the business or customer-contact trigger behind the abrupt volume increase beginning at 09:15.
Configure intraday alerts for material actual-to-forecast volume variance and rapidly rising occupancy.
Establish surge procedures such as overtime, reserve staffing, schedule adjustments, and cross-queue skill activation.
Reforecast remaining intervals immediately when sustained demand materially exceeds plan and recalculate staffing requirements.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Logged-in staffing stayed at 49 and productive staffing remained at 45–46, with no incident-time reduction.
Adherence remained stable between 91.84% and 93.88% and did not decline at incident onset.
Aggregate AHT remained close to the approximately 372–379 second forecast and did not show a sustained increase coincident with the service failure.
No routing event was recorded, transfer rates remained near their established levels, and elevated demand affected multiple queues.
Queue staffing allocations were unchanged and degradation was broad rather than isolated to one persistently overloaded queue.
No agents were recorded in training during any interval.
No platform event was recorded, and calls continued to be answered at high absolute volumes.

The immediate operational trigger was a discrete surge in actual arrivals beginning at 09:15; pre-incident actual volume closely matched forecast, supporting unexpected demand rather than a persistent forecasting bias.
Reported service levels reconcile with the supplied formula, and aggregate offered-call counts reconcile with queue-level totals.

stakeholder_summary: CC-001 was caused by an unexpected and sustained demand spike beginning at 09:15. Offered calls were approximately 56% above forecast through 11:45 while staffing, adherence, AHT, and queue allocations remained stable. Demand exceeded available capacity, producing 100% occupancy, longer waits, abandonment, and sustained service-level degradation.
